title: Service Boundary Network Hardening Guide (RBAC v2, Audit & SIEM Evidence)
summary: Practical guide for securing service boundaries in private deployments. Covers VPC segmentation patterns, firewall rule baselines, mTLS service identity model, RBAC v2 mapping for network operations, audit log schema for SIEM export, and an automated evidence pipeline checklist for compliance reviews.
body:
Purpose and scope:
This doc is a hands-on reference for engineering and security reviewers preparing private deployments (VPC/VPN/on-prem) for compliance audits. It focuses on the network/security boundary: how we carve up VPCs, what baseline firewall rules look like, how services authenticate mTLS, how RBAC v2 is applied to network operators and automation, and how audit logs are shaped for downstream SIEM ingestion and evidence automation.

Goals:
- Ensure least-privilege connectivity between service tiers and tenant/infra boundaries.
- Provide a stable, reviewable audit trail for both human reviewers and automated evidence consumers.
- Enable reproducible evidence exports (daily snapshots + on-demand) for internal/external compliance checks.
- Make operator roles explicit in RBAC v2 so approvals and emergency overrides are auditable.

Assumptions and constraints:
- Customer private deployments use cloud VPCs or equivalent on-prem segmented networks.
- Control plane connectivity (console, telemetry) uses separate management subnets and bastion jump hosts.
- We rely on the service mesh for intra-cluster encryption; this doc assumes mTLS for service-to-service where possible.
- Compliance: SOC2/ISO27001 style evidence required; timeline for producing evidence is 24 hours from request.

Recommended VPC segmentation patterns (quick reference):
1) Service-subnet-per-application (SSPA):
   - Each application (service group) gets its own subnet and security group.
   - Ingress to public-facing subnets via well-scoped ingress LB + ALB rules.
   - East-west access must go through explicitly allowed service proxies or mesh sidecars.
   - When to use: high multi-tenant risk with frequent deployments.

2) Tenant-isolation (logical tenants):
   - Separate VPCs per tenant for regulated customers (recommended for PCI/PHI).
   - Shared infra services (monitoring, auth) live in a central VPC and expose minimal egress APIs with allowlisted addresses.

3) Egress-proxy-only pattern:
   - Instances or containers have no direct internet egress; outbound goes through an egress proxy with allowlist and SIEM-forwarding.
   - Useful for strict data exfiltration controls.

Firewall baseline (stateful rules example):
- Default-deny inbound at all subnet boundaries.
- Allow lists only: allow TCP 443 from loadbalancer CIDR to service subnet for public endpoints.
- Control plane (admin) only: SSH (or SSM), HTTPS to management endpoints from corporate IP ranges or VPN.
- Service-to-service: allow only the necessary ports and only between service subnets that are authorized in policy.
- Egress: block everything by default, allow known telemetry/registry endpoints, and force through egress proxy.
- Example concrete rule names (for audit):
  - fw-allow-ingress-alb-443-production
  - fw-allow-mgmt-https-corp-vpn
  - fw-deny-all-other-ingress

mTLS service identity model (recommended):
- Use an internal CA (or private PKI) issuing short-lived certificates (max 24h auto-rotate for workloads).
- Identity = service:<namespace>:<service-name>. Example CN: service:payments:ingress-proxy.
- Verification: services validate both SAN and certificate issuer chain.
- Rotation: automated cert renewal via cert-agent; key material never persisted on disk in plain text.
- Fallback: for legacy non-mTLS services, place them in a restricted compatibility subnet and put a gateway that terminates TLS with strict logging.

RBAC v2 mapping for network & evidence operators:
- Roles (minimal recommended):
  - network-reader: can view firewall rules, network diagrams, and audit logs (read-only).
  - network-operator: can propose firewall changes, create draft rules in staging, view evidence exports. Requires two-step approval to apply to prod.
  - network-admin: can apply approved changes and manage egress proxies (audit logging enabled). Limited to <10 members.
  - evidence-automation: service account used by pipelines to generate evidence bundles and push to SIEM or evidence storage.
- Policies:
  - All change actions require an associated ticket ID in the change metadata and must trigger a log entry with before/after snapshots.
  - Emergency changes must be flagged and automatically generate a post-hoc evidence collection.

Audit log schema (schema oriented for SIEM-friendly lines):
- Each network/audit event is emitted as a single JSON line with the following top-level fields:
  - timestamp (ISO8601 UTC)
  - event_id (UUIDv4)
  - src (string): system emitting the event (firewall, egress-proxy, cert-agent, rbac-service)
  - action (string): e.g., firewall.create, firewall.update, mTLS.issue, rbac.grant, evidence.export
  - actor (string): principal (user:alice OR svc:evidence-automation)
  - resource (string): resource identifier e.g., fw-rule-id, subnet-id, cert-id
  - outcome (string): success | failure | partial
  - diff (string): brief JSON-encoded before/after or change summary (optional, but keep as compact string)
  - request_id (string): correlates across systems for a tenant request
- Sample log line (single-line JSON):
  {"timestamp":"2026-02-14T17:23:45Z","event_id":"8a3f9b2e-4c12-4a66-9b1a-123456789abc","src":"firewall-service","action":"firewall.update","actor":"user:diego.rivera","resource":"fw-allow-ingress-alb-443-production","outcome":"success","diff":"{"before":"deny","after":"allow 443 from ALB"}","request_id":"JIRA-6789"}

SIEM export and transform guidance:
- Export pipeline: logs -> log-shipper (filebeat/td-agent) -> central collector -> transform -> SIEM index.
- Transform rules: ensure timestamp normalization to UTC, map actor to canonical identity (user: or svc:), and parse diff into a compact field for quick search.
- Tagging: add tags {environment:production|staging, team:network, tenant:<id>} for every event.
- Retention: keep raw logs for 90 days, parsed indices for 365 days, evidence snapshots (bundles) stored per-audit for minimum 2 years or per contract.

Evidence automation (high-level playbook):
1) Daily snapshot job (k8s cronjob or airflow):
   - Collect firewall config (API dump), network ACLs, subnet routing tables, active certs, RBAC role bindings.
   - Produce a signed tarball and upload to evidence-bucket/environment/date/{bundle}.
   - Publish metadata: bundle checksum, items included, generated_by, time range.
2) On-demand audit export (triggered from ticket):
   - Validate ticket ID and requester role.
   - Re-run snapshot with extended logs (last 30d), include SIEM query results for correlated events and any emergency change flags.
   - Mark bundle with audit-request-id and notify reviewers via pre-configured channel.
3) Verification tests (automated):
   - Smoke test: ensure egress-proxy only allows known domains.
   - Cert test: pick random running workload, validate certificate chain and expiration window.
   - Rule test: replay a synthetic connection from staging subnet to ensure deny rules are enforced.

Operational runbook (short):
- Routine change flow: propose -> review (network-operator + security reviewer) -> apply in staging -> canary traffic -> apply to prod with network-admin approval.
- Emergency flow: apply change with emergency flag -> automated evidence snapshot -> post-mortem ticket and 48-hour remediation window.

Textual diagram (ASCII) - quick reference (replace with architectural diagram for final):
  Internet
    |
   ALB (ingress) -- fw-allow-ingress-alb-443 --> Public subnet (ingress proxies)
    |                              |
    |-- egress-proxy --> NAT --> Internet (restricted)
    |                              |
   Service mesh (mTLS) <---> App subnets <---> Tenant VPCs (peering or transit gateway)
    |
   Management VPC: bastion + logging -> SIEM collector

Hardening checklist (actionable items, include verification commands where applicable):
- [ ] Default-deny inbound at subnet boundaries (verify: review security group/ACL rules, command: `aws ec2 describe-security-groups --filters Name=tag:env,Values=prod` and check no 0.0.0.0/0 rules except ALB).
- [ ] Egress goes through proxy (verify: probe container network namespace, curl --proxy and check headers).
- [ ] mTLS enabled between services (verify: pick endpoint and `openssl s_client -connect svc-host:port -showcerts` and validate CN format).
- [ ] Short-lived workload certs (verify: cert expiration < 48h).
- [ ] RBAC v2 roles limit network-admin members to <10 (verify: `rbac-cli list-role-members network-admin`).
- [ ] All firewall changes reference JIRA ticket in audit log (verify by searching SIEM for missing request_id fields).
- [ ] Daily evidence snapshot job status green for last 7 days (verify: check evidence pipeline health endpoint).
- [ ] SIEM ingestion complete and parsable (verify: sample query for event types from last 24h).

Notes & open questions (left for follow-up):
- Do we want to standardize on a single cert agent implementation across cloud and on-prem? (Asha to prototype).
- Should evidence bundles be immutable and replicated to cold storage for multi-year retention? Cost estimate needed.
- Mapping between RBAC v2 identities and corporate SSO groups needs a documented sync flow (Priya).

Appendix: quick grep-able snippets and helpful commands:
- Dump firewall rules (AWS): `aws ec2 describe-network-acls --filters Name=tag:env,Values=prod`
- Generate evidence bundle (local dev): `./tools/evidence/collect --env prod --ticket JIRA-6789`
- Sample SIEM query (ELK): `index:network-logs AND src:firewall-service AND action:firewall.update AND request_id:JIRA-6789`

Last updated by Morgan Chen. If anything is unclear, ping #private-deployments on Slack or add a comment to JIRA-6789.
